title: Verify and close the task planning foundation
request: Continue TP-01E only: verify the complete hierarchical planning foundation, repair gate-required issues, and decide whether the model-proposal package may begin.
spec: engineering/planning/TP_01E.txt and all nine items in the master TP-01 acceptance checklist. No task execution, model purpose, UI or default rollout.
plan: Recheck the current source inventories and portable contract boundary.
Exercise the actual lean agent environment and prevent eager ML imports.
Strengthen adapter zero-call evidence and verify it detects swallowed runtime attempts.
Run the installed wheel, schemas, existing compatibility regressions and provisioned package/milestone gates.
Obtain independent review, record exact results and publish validated development-corpus output.

decisions.decision: Retain the already-lazy agent_metrics import rather than refactoring it.
decisions.why: The observed historical regression was already fixed; only a missing regression test needed work.

decisions.decision: Use fresh subprocesses with an import blocker in both Python environments.
decisions.why: The suite preloads ML modules before forking; an ordinary in-process test could hide an accidental eager import.

decisions.decision: Assert zero calls on actual stored registry handlers and runtime owners, in addition to raising on invocation.
decisions.why: A caught exception or blocked fallback could conceal a forbidden planning side effect.

decisions.decision: Keep every item in the actual nine-row master checklist.
decisions.why: The E prompt says seven items but the supplied master actually lists nine; dropping two would weaken acceptance.

decisions.decision: Keep scientific owners, schemas, public contract versions and app defaults unchanged.
decisions.why: This is foundation verification, not another execution or orchestration implementation.

change: Adds two import-boundary tests and strengthens two adapter purity tests. Documents combined architecture, ownership, contract identities and honest gate results. Production code is unchanged in TP-01E.

findings.defect: Existing adapter purity tests could miss a forbidden call if its raised exception was caught.
findings.scenario: A metadata helper attempted a project write, caught the test spy exception and continued to return a mapped graph.
findings.cause: The original tests installed raising spies but discarded the mapping result and did not assert zero calls.
findings.fix: Require mapped output and valid graph, spy stored handlers, registry, guards, both storage writers, table and holdout owners and gateway, and assert every call count is zero.
findings.test: A controlled swallowed-write fault now makes the strengthened purity test fail as expected; unmodified source passes all forty-one adapter tests.

findings.defect: There was no fresh-process regression test preventing the historical eager core import in the lean harness.
findings.scenario: A future top-level core import in agent_metrics would load unavailable ML libraries in the separate campaign environment, while preloaded suite workers might conceal it.
findings.cause: The production import was already lazy but the lean separation lacked explicit negative-control coverage.
findings.fix: Add subprocess tests that forbid even attempted core and ML imports while importing the harness and using in-memory metrics.
findings.test: Two tests passed in both provided environments. Deliberate eager core, numpy and sklearn imports fail with the blocker marker.

findings.defect: The E prompt describes seven checklist items, but the master contains nine.
findings.scenario: A literal seven-row report would omit honest regression reporting and the final readiness decision.
findings.cause: The prompt count is inconsistent with its referenced checklist.
findings.fix: Preserve all nine master items and explain the discrepancy in the report.
findings.test: Manual source comparison confirms all nine criteria appear in the acceptance table.

findings.defect: The initial focused command used tests-directory paths that the current runner does not accept.
findings.scenario: The runner rejected all requested names before collecting any tests.
findings.cause: The current runner expects file basenames, optionally without the Python suffix.
findings.fix: Read the current runner parser and rerun with its accepted basename format.
findings.test: The rejected command ran no tests; corrected focused results are recorded separately.

findings.defect: The drafted report grouped WorkflowRun with owners of mutable execution state.
findings.scenario: A reader could treat its derived report-done status as proof that a physical export was produced.
findings.cause: The report grouped an evidence readback contract with orchestration and checkpoint controllers.
findings.fix: Document WorkflowRun separately as derived readback and retain stage/programme records, jobs and orchestration/checkpoints as mutable owners.
findings.test: The reviewer checked the current builder and confirmed that the corrected report resolves the finding; no production source change was needed.

outcome: TP-01E complete. The whole TP-01 architecture/contracts/validation/metadata-adapter foundation is verified. The full file suite ran 5348 tests with 14 existing skips; PostgreSQL ran 5350 with 11 existing skips; no failures or new skipped tests. Focused, package, schema, isolated wheel, actual lean environment and final independent review checks pass. Reviewed records were regenerated through validated staged output and all four corpus checks passed; the final record is regenerated and checked again before publication. Core 0.157.0, runtime owners, model purposes, dependencies, Home/Lead Agent behavior and defaults are unchanged. TP-02 may begin as a separate proposal-only package and has not started. Execution, durable recovery, runtime identity/approval checks and full measured evidence remain later work. The unrelated store catalog edit is preserved.
lessons: A raising test spy is insufficient when application code may catch exceptions; assert the call count.
Use fresh interpreters for import-boundary tests in a suite that preloads libraries before forking.
Do not duplicate a historical fix that is already present in the current source.
Read the actual checklist rather than trusting an inconsistent item count.
risks: A mapped graph could be mistaken for execution permission or completed evidence.
Lean imports could accidentally acquire ML dependencies.
Incomplete reporting could hide skipped or failed environment checks.
The prior generated-corpus byte damage has an unconfirmed origin; validate staged generator output before publishing.
